sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 covers the western half of Lenola, the village in the west of Moorestown Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north about 30 degrees to the right of the top of the page. Lenola Road runs down the right edge; Camden Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet diagonally from the north-west and meets Lenola Road at the upper right, where New Albany Road branches off to the north-east. Claypool and Cottage Avenue bound the narrow lots north of Camden Avenue at the top of the sheet. South of Camden Avenue lies a small grid of residential streets: Winthrop Avenue, which runs as a loop around the development, Lincoln Avenue, Garfield Avenue and Emerson Avenue, with Beacon Street meeting Lenola Road at the right edge. The blocks are laid out in narrow house lots, most built up with one- and two-storey frame dwellings, auto houses and coops; several lots are still empty. Commercial use is limited to a group of stores and a gasoline filling station around the Camden Avenue and Lenola Road corner and a second filling station further west on Camden Avenue. A strip of pasted correction slips covers the lots along the upper Winthrop Avenue. The western third of the sheet is mostly empty swamp land along the North Branch of Pensauken Creek, which also marks the line between Chester Township and Moorestown Township. Water pipes with their diameters and fire hydrants are drawn along most streets. The sheet adjoins sheet 28 to the north, sheet 29 to the north-east and sheet 27 to the east.
notes: Winthrop Avenue is drawn as one loop; today its upper segments between Lincoln Avenue and Lenola Road and west of Lincoln Avenue are Whittier Avenue, and its western north-south leg is Grant Avenue.

Lincoln Avenue and Garfield Avenue are now South Lincoln Avenue and South Garfield Avenue; Lenola Road is North and South Lenola Road; Camden Avenue west of Lenola Road is West Camden Avenue; Claypool is Claypoole Avenue.
The Grant Avenue and Whittier Avenue corner was excluded from the fit: the drawn junction is about 5 m from the modern one.
Sheet dated June 1929, published as part of the Moorestown atlas.

Lenola west of Lenola Road: Camden Av, New Albany Rd, Claypool, Cottage Av, Winthrop Av (loop; upper segments now Whittier Avenue, west leg now Grant Avenue), Lincoln Av, Garfield Av, Emerson Av; North Branch Pensauken Creek and swamp land to the west. 100 ft scale, one part, north about 30 degrees right of up.

sheet-27-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 27 is the main map of the sheet, covering the east side of Lenola Road in Lenola, Moorestown Township, at 100 feet to an inch with north about 24 degrees to the right of the top of the page. Lenola Road runs down the left side of the part from its crossing with Camden Avenue at the top left to the wooden bridge over the North Branch of Pensauken Creek near the bottom; Emerson Avenue, Beacon and Winthrop Avenue meet it from either side. Camden Avenue crosses the top of the part towards the east. Between Camden Avenue and Beacon lie Villa Avenue and Revere Avenue, lined with narrow house lots and frame dwellings, many still vacant. The densest buildings are on Camden Avenue near Lenola Road: the Lenola Community Centre, a row of stores, a garage with a concrete floor and a plumbing shop, with gasoline tanks along the street front. The north side of Camden Avenue east of the stores is open woods with scattered houses, and an unnamed cemetery lies south of Camden Avenue at the right. South of Beacon the land is mostly open, with a few dwellings and coops along Lenola Road. The creek at the bottom marks the boundary between Moorestown Township and Chester Township. The part is bounded on the lower right by a heavy line enclosing part 2, which shows Lenola Road further south; the margins are marked 'No exposure'. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along Lenola Road and Camden Avenue.
notes: Lenola Road is now North and South Lenola Road; Beacon is Beacon Street.
The drawn Lenola Road junctions with Beacon, Winthrop Avenue and Villa Avenue carry residuals of 3.7 to 5 m; they were kept, as the detected points lie on the drawn street centres.
Devon Avenue, a modern street crossing Camden Avenue east of the cemetery, is not drawn and was not used.

Lenola east of Lenola Road. Two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 (main) Camden Av, Villa Av, Revere Av, Beacon, Emerson and Winthrop stubs, cemetery, Pensauken Creek; part 2 (lower right, own north arrow) Lenola Rd south to Kings Highway or Haddonfield Av, Ivy Av, Palmer (not opened), Regenhard. 100 ft scale.

sheet-27-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 27 is a separately oriented block in the lower right of the sheet, enclosed by a heavy line and carrying its own north arrow, about 53 degrees to the right of the top of the page. It shows Lenola Road further south, from below Beacon down to Kings Highway, also called Haddonfield Avenue, which crosses the bottom of the part. East of Lenola Road a small subdivision is laid out: Ivy Avenue runs east from Lenola Road and turns south as Regenhard, which returns to Kings Highway; Palmer, marked 'not opened', crosses the middle of the tract. The lots are narrow and only partly built, with frame dwellings and auto houses mostly along Lenola Road and the north side of Ivy Avenue. A gasoline filling station and a dwelling with a store stand at the Kings Highway corner of Lenola Road. The North Branch of Pensauken Creek winds down the right side of the part through open land, and the line between Chester Township and Moorestown Township follows Lenola Road. A twelve-inch water main runs along Kings Highway towards Moorestown. Lenola Road is drawn about 100 feet wide at Kings Highway although it is lettered 60 and 65 feet. The margins next to the main part and along the right edge are marked 'No exposure'.
notes: Placed from only four points (two detected, two hand-picked) with an affine fit; low confidence.
Regenhard is now Regenhard Avenue; Lenola Road is South Lenola Road; Kings Highway keeps its name.
Palmer, not opened in 1929, has no modern counterpart in the reference data.
Modern Ivy Avenue curves into Regenhard Avenue where the sheet draws a square corner.

Lenola east of Lenola Road. Two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 (main) Camden Av, Villa Av, Revere Av, Beacon, Emerson and Winthrop stubs, cemetery, Pensauken Creek; part 2 (lower right, own north arrow) Lenola Rd south to Kings Highway or Haddonfield Av, Ivy Av, Palmer (not opened), Regenhard. 100 ft scale.

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 covers the north-western part of Lenola, Moorestown Township, west of Lenola Road, at 100 feet to an inch with north about 30 degrees to the right of the top of the page. Lenola Road runs down the right side of the sheet. Across the top, Pine runs between scattered houses, with sewage disposal beds in the upper left corner and a creek crossing the sheet diagonally to a wood bridge under Lenola Road. Below it Harding Avenue, Lincoln Avenue, Garfield Avenue and Wilson form a small grid of narrow house lots, densely built with one- and two-storey frame dwellings, some of concrete block; an unnamed street west of Lincoln Avenue is lettered 'not named' and 'not open'. The Pennsylvania Railroad's Amboy Division crosses the middle of the sheet diagonally on a concrete bridge over the North Branch of Pensauken Creek, with the Lenola passenger station, a siding and coal pile and R. W. Johnson's coal and wood yard beside Moore near Lenola Road. South of the railroad, Cottage Avenue, Browning and Claypool bound a second group of lots with dwellings, coops and the Pentecostal Church on Lenola Road; the open land to the west is swamp land along the creek, which marks the line between Chester Township and Moorestown Township. Camden Avenue crosses the bottom left corner. Moore St. and Merion St. are lettered as short stubs east of Lenola Road. The top margin is marked 'No exposure'. The sheet adjoins sheet 29 to the east and sheet 26 to the south.
notes: Renamed since: Lenola Road is North Lenola Road; Lincoln Avenue and Garfield Avenue are North Lincoln Avenue and North Garfield Avenue; Wilson is West Wilson Avenue; Browning is Browning Avenue; Claypool is Claypoole Avenue; Pine is Pine Street; Merion St. is Merion Avenue; Camden Avenue here is West Camden Avenue.
The P.R.R. Amboy Division line survives in the reference data as the Pemberton Industrial Track; its crossing with Lenola Road was used as a control point.
Moore west of Lenola Road, along the railroad, has no modern counterpart; Marion Avenue, a modern street between Wilson and the railroad, is not drawn.
The Pine Street junction with Lenola Road lies at the top edge of the sheet and was excluded.

Lenola north-west: Pine, Harding Av, Wilson, Lincoln Av, Garfield Av, Lenola Rd, P.R.R. (Amboy Div.) with Lenola passenger station, Moore, Browning, Cottage Av, Claypool, Camden Av corner. 100 ft scale, one part.

sheet-29-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 29 is the main map of the sheet, covering the north-eastern part of Lenola, Moorestown Township, east of Lenola Road, at 100 feet to an inch with north about 53 degrees to the right of the top of the page. Lenola Road runs diagonally up the left side, with short stubs of Wilson St., Moore St., Browning St. and Claypool St. lettered on its west side. New Albany Road crosses the bottom of the part. Between them lies a grid of residential streets: Wilson, Moore, Errickson and Winstead run across the part and are crossed by Harvey Avenue and Grand Avenue; the blocks are divided into narrow house lots, densely built with one- and two-storey frame dwellings along Wilson and Moore and more thinly to the south. The Pennsylvania Railroad's Amboy Division crosses the part diagonally from Lenola Road to New Albany Road, with Merion running beside it. Along the railroad stand the Gospel Tabernacle and the Camden Mfg. Co., makers of wood turnings. On New Albany Road are the Lenola Public School, a brick school, the Lenola Public School first grade building, the Lenola Union Church and the Lenola Volunteer Fire Co. No. 1 with its siren tower near Lenola Road. A large open tract south of the railroad, block 126, is almost empty. The part is separated from the strip along Center Street at the top of the sheet (part 2) by a heavy line, and its upper margin is marked 'No exposure'. Water mains of 6 and 12 inches and hydrants are drawn along most streets.
notes: Renamed since: Lenola Road is North Lenola Road; Wilson is East Wilson Avenue (West Wilson Avenue west of Lenola Road); Errickson and Winstead are Errickson Avenue and Winstead Avenue; Browning St. is Browning Avenue; Claypool St. is Claypoole Avenue.
Harvey Avenue has no modern counterpart in the reference data.

Modern Merion Avenue no longer follows the drawn Merion beside the railroad east of Lenola Road; its junctions with Winstead, Errickson, Grand and New Albany were rejected or excluded (13 to 16 m off). The railroad itself survives as the Pemberton Industrial Track.
The modern nodes of Wilson at Lenola Road (East and West Wilson Avenue) lie 4 to 9 m from the drawn junction and were excluded.

Lenola north-east. Two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 (main, lower) Lenola Rd, Wilson, Moore, Errickson, Winstead, New Albany Rd, Harvey Av, Grand Av, P.R.R. (Amboy Div.), Lenola Public School; part 2 (top strip, own north arrow) Center St east of Lenola Rd, Pine St stub. 100 ft scale.

sheet-29-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 29 is a narrow strip across the top of the sheet, separated from the main map by a heavy line and carrying its own north arrow. It shows Center, a long straight street running east from Lenola Road, which crosses the left end of the strip, with Pine St. meeting Lenola Road just below. The strip is drawn at 100 feet to an inch; north lies about 50 degrees to the right of the top of the page. The lots on both sides of Center are long and narrow and only partly built, with one- and two-storey frame dwellings, a few stores and auto houses, and many vacant lots, especially towards the east; house numbers run from 1 near Lenola Road to 316 at the east end. A six-inch water pipe runs along Center from Lenola Road. Both the top margin and the line along the bottom of the strip are marked 'No exposure', and the strip reaches the right edge of the sheet without a crossing street. The area south of the strip is drawn on sheet 28 and in part 1 of this sheet.
notes: Placed from one detected junction (Center and Lenola Road) with the scale assumed from the rest of the atlas (4.0 px per ft) and the rotation of the drawn lines (about 50 degrees, matching modern Center Street); low confidence, errors grow towards the east end of the strip.
Center is now Center Street; Lenola Road is North Lenola Road.
The Pine Street junction, 37 m from Center Street, was left out: as a second point it gave a scale 8 percent off.

Lenola north-east. Two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 (main, lower) Lenola Rd, Wilson, Moore, Errickson, Winstead, New Albany Rd, Harvey Av, Grand Av, P.R.R. (Amboy Div.), Lenola Public School; part 2 (top strip, own north arrow) Center St east of Lenola Rd, Pine St stub. 100 ft scale.
